n8f1608f7159c: Introduction/Background: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) is critical step for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest survival. Pre-medical students represent an unstudied and high-potential bystander population, yet predictors of post-training CPR willingness remain poorly characterized. Hypothesis: Pre-medical students from a public university in Argentina perceiving CPR training as highly important would demonstrate greater willingness to perform CPR after course completion. Methods: Prospective, cross-sectional study post mandated CPR-course survey of all pre-medical students (full cohort 2026) at Universidad Nacional de La Matanza, Argentina. The educational program comprised a 3-hour, theoretical-practical course led by university instructors in accordance with the 2025 AHA guidelines. Variables included demographics, prior CPR exposure (awareness, prior formal course, real-life CPR performance), perceived training importance (Likert 1-5), post-course CPR willingness (Likert 1-5; high=4-5). Real-life CPR performance was operationally defined as the delivery of chest compressions with or without the use of an automated external defibrillator (AED). Bivariate analyses used chi-square and crude odds ratios (OR, 95%CI). Two multivariable logistic regression models identified independent factors associated to: Model 1: high post-course CPR willingness and model 2: prior real-life CPR performance. Results: 448 students responded (mean age 21.9±5.5 years; 70.8% female). Prior awareness of CPR was high (94.9%); 32.1% had completed a prior formal CPR course; only 6.5% had performed CPR in a real-life emergency. Perceived importance was: 96.2% rated 5/5. High post-course CPR willingness was reported by 67.2%. In bivariate analysis, maximum importance perception was associated with high willingness to render CPR in real life (OR=3.07, 95%CI:1.14-8.23, p=0.020), as was prior formal CPR course (OR=1.82, 95%CI:1.16-2.84, p=0.008). In multivariable analysis (Model 1), maximum importance perception independently predicted high willingness (adjusted OR=2.96, 95%CI:1.07-8.22, p=0.037). For real-life CPR performance (Model 2), prior formal CPR course (adjusted OR=5.24, 95%CI:2.06-13.36, p<0.001) and older age (adjusted OR=2.18 per SD, 95%CI:1.63-2.92, p<0.001) were the sole independent predictors. Gender was not associated with either outcome. Conclusions: Perceiving CPR training as maximally important independently predicted greater willingness to perform CPR post-course. Prior formal CPR training was the strongest predictor of real-life CPR performance. These findings support early, repeated CPR training in medical curricula and emphasize framing instruction within clinical relevance to enhance motivation and real-world application. These cross-sectional associations warrant confirmation in longitudinal studies.
nd3d17a352c59: US veterans represent a large and diverse population with distinctive demographic characteristics, comorbidity profiles, and social determinants of health shaped by military service. These factors contribute to a high burden of cardiovascular risk and low attainment of ideal cardiovascular health. At the same time, the Department of Veterans Affairs, which operates the nation’s largest integrated healthcare system, provides a unique infrastructure for delivering population-level cardiovascular disease prevention for veterans. Understanding its successes and ongoing challenges can inform broader strategies across all health systems for promoting health among veterans. This scientific statement applies the American Heart Association’s Life’s Essential 8 framework, expanded to include mental health and substance use, to evaluate veteran cardiovascular health. For each domain, we review guideline recommendations, barriers to achieving optimal health, and major Veterans Affairs programs such as Patient Aligned Care Teams, the MOVE! Weight Management Program for Veterans, Whole Health, telehealth-based interventions, and integrated mental health and substance use disorder services. Across domains, veterans receiving Veterans Affairs care often achieve outcomes that are equal to or better than those of their non–Veterans Affairs counterparts, reflecting the strengths of the system in coordinated, team-based care and research-driven implementation. Despite substantial progress, opportunities remain to improve veteran lifestyle behaviors, metabolic health, lipid and blood pressure control, engagement in mental health and substance use care, and detection and management of sleep disorders. Addressing these challenges at the Veterans Affairs will require continuing to expand care access, enhancing digital data integration, tailoring interventions to high-risk subgroups, and strengthening implementation strategies to improve uptake and engagement across Veterans Affairs services.
n84cf2bfdaf24: ObjectivesTo evaluate trends in pregabalin use and overdose in Australia and examine temporal relationships with media coverage (December 2018), prescribing and dispensing restrictions (April 2020), and boxed warnings (February 2021).DesignRetrospective observational study of dispensing and overdose data, with changepoint, interrupted time series, and latent class analysis.Setting and participantsPharmaceutical Benefits Scheme data (PBS; 10% random sample of people with drug subsidies) and overdose calls (self-harm, recreational use, and misuse) reported to Australia’s largest Poisons Centre (50% national sample), 2016-24.Main outcome measuresPopulation adjusted rates of dispensing and overdose, timing of breakpoints and rate ratios, proportion of people who use pregabalin at high risk of misuse.Results227 864 people were dispensed 3 441 851 pregabalin prescriptions in the PBS 10% sample and 4871 pregabalin overdose calls were made to the Poisons Centre. Pregabalin use peaked in 2018 before plateauing and declining. Three breakpoints were found in dispensing data, with major decreases in level and slope: December 2018, May 2020, December 2021. The combined rate ratio for dispensing was 0.748 (95% confidence interval 0.700 to 0.800). Compared with the projected historical trend in the absence of interventions (counterfactual), approximately 118 390 (93 960 to 140 940) fewer pregabalin prescriptions were recorded nationally in December 2021, and an ongoing reduction of 0.7% (0.5% to 0.9%) was found each month. All breakpoints were associated with declines in overdose rates, with a combined rate ratio of 0.532 (95% CI 0.406 to 0.695). This reduction corresponded to approximately 41.3 (26.9 to 52.4) fewer pregabalin overdose calls in December 2021 and an ongoing reduction of 1.6% (1.0% to 2.3%) each month. Latent class analysis of 57 744 people dispensed pregabalin in the 12 months after the final breakpoint revealed four groups. The high risk group (7790, 13.5%) were more likely male, younger, dispensed more pregabalin, with shorter refill interval and high rates of opioids and benzodiazepine co-use (5120 (65.7%) and 2455 (31.5%), respectively).ConclusionsPregabalin use and overdose in Australia have declined in recent years. Major decreases in trend corresponded with media coverage (December 2018) and prescribing and dispensing restrictions (May 2020). The third breakpoint may be a delayed impact of boxed warnings (implemented February 2021). These findings suggest that regulatory and risk communication measures may contribute to reducing pregabalin related harm.

n1fa0803fb276: Human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)–derived cardiomyocytes (iPSC cardiomyocytes) as a model for cardiac disease have become increasingly important, bolstered by the Food and Drug Administration’s initiative to promote novel alternative methods for biomedical research. A key limitation of metabolically immature iPSC cardiomyocytes is their limited ability to accurately recapitulate mitochondria-dependent pathologies, such as Friedreich ataxia–associated cardiomyopathy. Adult cardiomyocytes are characterized by a high density of interfibrillar mitochondria, abundant respiratory complexes (I–V) that form supercomplexes, and efficient utilization of fatty acids to drive mitochondrial respiration. These unique metabolic structures and functions are largely missing in iPSC cardiomyocytes. Further, whether iPSC cardiomyocytes can efficiently utilize fatty acids for respiration in the presence of glucose, a unique adult feature, remains unclear. We developed a chemically defined, 11-component maturation medium (MM11) designed using a bioinformatics-guided strategy that identified high-fidelity transcriptional markers of adult cardiac metabolic maturity. Human iPSC cardiomyocytes were treated with MM11 for 2 weeks and evaluated at the molecular, structural, and functional levels, with an emphasis on mitochondrial maturity. We benchmarked our results with isolated primary adult human cardiomyocytes. Last, we tested whether this method could enable us to more accurately model Friedreich ataxia cardiomyopathy. MM11 treatment increased expression of metabolic pathways, including mitochondrial respiration and fatty acid metabolism, at the transcript and protein levels. Ultrastructural analyses revealed the formation of interfibrillar mitochondria and mitochondrial respiratory supercomplexes, a feature never shown in previous reports. Functionally, MM11-treated iPSC cardiomyocytes exhibited substantially increased oxidative phosphorylation and a metabolic preference for fatty acid utilization in the presence of physiologic substrates, as determined by oxygen consumption assays and 13 C isotope tracing. MM11 promotes robust metabolic maturation of human iPSC cardiomyocytes, enabling sophisticated mitochondrial architecture and substrate utilization. These metabolically matured cardiomyocytes more faithfully model mitochondria-dependent cardiac pathologies, including ischemia-reperfusion injury and Friedreich ataxia cardiomyopathy, improving the use of iPSC cardiomyocytes for mechanistic studies of human heart disease.
n0d6af8f867a0: Frailty is associated with worse outcomes after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). However, the comparative effectiveness of off-pump CABG (OPCAB) versus on-pump CABG (ONCAB) in prefrail and frail patients remains uncertain. This multicenter, randomized, open-label trial enrolled patients ≥60 years of age classified as prefrail or frail, randomized 1:1, between January 2018 and December 2024. The primary outcome was a 30-day composite of death, myocardial infarction, stroke, renal failure, acute respiratory distress syndrome, or reoperation for bleeding. Secondary outcomes included ventilation time, intensive care unit and hospital stay, transfusion requirements, completeness of revascularization, surgical wound infection at 30 days, and neurocognitive function preoperatively and at 1 year. Analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle; relative risks with 95% CIs were estimated. A total of 508 patients were included (OPCAB, n=258; ONCAB, n=250; median age, 68 years [interquartile range, 65.0–73]; 30.5% female). The primary composite outcome occurred in 28 patients receiving OPCAB (10.9%) and 40 patients receiving ONCAB (16.0%; relative risk, 1.47 [95% CI, 0.94–2.31]; P =0.09). Surgical wound infection was more frequent with ONCAB (20 [8.0%] versus 9 [3.5%]; P =0.04). No significant differences were observed in neurocognitive or quality of life outcomes at 1 year. Estimated 1-year survival probabilities were 96.1% and 92.8% in the OPCAB and ONCAB groups, respectively ( P =0.099). In prefrail and frail patients undergoing CABG, OPCAB and ONCAB resulted in similar rates of the primary composite outcome. No significant differences between OPCAB and ONCAB were found in neurocognitive outcomes. URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov ; Unique identifier: NCT02338947.

n00f7251c2a08: One of the most central animating questions in medicine is “What is the cause?” Clinicians assiduously seek the diagnosis of a patient’s perplexing symptoms or probe what pathophysiology underlies the disease. Poetry is similarly engaged in a quest for knowing and by its enlarging of the field of inquiry as to the deepest roots of human suffering, it is complementary to, and thus useful in, medical practice. In the poem “Etiology,” medical language (“neoplastic transformation,” “terminology”) is placed beside unscientific explanatory systems (“feng shui,” “fortune stick[s]”), suggesting that illness may arise from several causal worlds at once. A malignancy may be cellular, environmental, familial, cultural, and even spiritual, depending on the kind of history being taken and by whom. “[A]bbreviations and poor penmanship” evokes the insufficiency patients may feel when their illness is summarily translated into clinical shorthand or technical jargon; poetry re-expands the diagnostic arena, restoring texture and richness to causation (“…white rice you relish/is it incense you burnt for your parents, black/on your fingertips blooming dust on the wall”). The poem’s cascading interrogatives become like a differential diagnosis, its syntax and persistent rhetorical questioning resembling good clinical reasoning. Yet the poem tolerates uncertainty, without discounting rigor. In the end, “Etiology” does not oppose medicine’s pursuit of an explanation, but rather amplifies it: “is it the blood you own, now rushing back to you again?” it concludes without really concluding, helping us understand that merely naming or owning is never the end of our questions.

n2b03ac0944f4: A remarkable era in acute ischemic stroke care is now coming to a close—the period of the “reperfusion revolution.” Over the past few decades, pharmacological and mechanical flow restoration therapies became steadily more effective. By restoring blood flow and terminating the ischemic period, reperfusion salvages those cerebral tissues not yet irreversibly injured. However, the reperfusion strategy in acute stroke care is now reaching its limits. Current endovascular thrombectomy approaches reopen over 85% of occluded arteries, leaving little scope for further advance. And successful reperfusion treatment alone clearly only partially solves the therapeutic challenge. Among patients with ischemic stroke due to large-vessel occlusion who receive endovascular thrombectomy, more than two-thirds nevertheless have a disabled final outcome. Restoring blood flow yields incomplete recoveries because some irreversible injury accrues before recanalization can be achieved and additional injury is generated by reperfusion itself. To fully eradicate stroke-related disability, complementary therapies are needed, including: bridging neuroprotection agents, which allow brain cells to tolerate ischemia until reperfusion is attained; reperfusion neuroprotection agents, which avert reperfusion injury; and neuroreparative agents, which promote postinjury reorganization of neurons and synapses.

n409415d3cfa3: Background: Transthyretin-lowering therapies target the underlying cause of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM), but their effects on myocardial amyloid burden and cardiac remodelling remain incompletely characterized. We evaluated the myocardial effects of sustained transthyretin suppression with eplontersen using serial multiparametric cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR). Methods: This CMR study was a pre-specified, international, prospective study embedded within the randomized, placebo-controlled phase 3 CARDIO-TTRansform trial. Participants underwent CMR at baseline and planned assessments at weeks 25, 49, 97, and 140. The primary imaging analysis evaluated longitudinal changes in CMR parameters using mixed models for repeated measures. Myocardial amyloid regression and progression were defined as ≥5 percentage-point decreases and increases in extracellular volume (ECV), respectively. All other patients were considered stable. Results: We enrolled 120 participants with baseline and ≥1 follow-up CMR assessment (eplontersen, n=58; placebo, n=62; mean age, 76.7±6.5 years; 95% male; baseline stabilizer, 12.5%). At week 140 eplontersen resulted in lower ECV, compared with placebo (least-squares mean difference [95% CI], –6.7 percentage points [ –8.7 to –4.7]; P<0.001) and lower native T1 ( –25.9ms [–41.7 to –10.2 ]; P=0.002) and left ventricular mass (–19.1g [–28.0 to –10.2]; P<0.001). Eplontersen also increased left ventricular ejection fraction (+5.1% [1.8–8.3]; P=0.002), right ventricular ejection fraction (+4.6% [0.6–8.7]; P=0.03), and left ventricular global longitudinal, circumferential, and radial strain and right ventricular longitudinal strain (all P<0.05), compared to placebo. At week-140, myocardial amyloid regression occurred in 12.5% receiving eplontersen versus 0% receiving placebo, whereas progression occurred in 12.5% versus 76%, respectively. Conclusions: Sustained transthyretin suppression with eplontersen resulted in substantially lower myocardial ECV and favorable changes in cardiac structure, biventricular systolic function, and myocardial deformation compared with placebo in a cohort of patients mostly not on background stabilizer at baseline. These findings provide randomized evidence that lowering circulating transthyretin modifies myocardial disease progression in ATTR-CM and support serial multiparametric CMR for characterizing myocardial treatment response.
n3f1ba72f3b86: In participants with obesity with established cardiovascular disease or chronic kidney disease or at increased risk of cardiovascular disease, survodutide was not associated with increased risk for the primary composite endpoint of death from cardiovascular causes, non-fatal stroke, non-fatal myocardial infarction, ischaemia-related coronary revascularisation, or heart failure event compared with placebo. n52c11af6030e: Treatment with efinopegdutide resulted in a significantly greater proportion of participants with MASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis compared with placebo. n9aeab6436516: Background: Connexin 43 (Cx43) gap junctions are abnormally accumulated and lateralized in Atrial fibrillation (AF), however, the underlying mechanisms remain elusive. The purpose of this study is to explore the role of optineurin (OPTN), a selective autophagy receptor, in maintaining Cx43 homeostasis and protecting against AF. Methods: Firstly, three publicly available AF-related datasets were analyzed to evaluate the potential relationship of OPTN with AF. Then, to examine whether OPTN-mediated selective autophagy is involved in regulating the fate of Cx43 in AF, Co-IP and immunofluorescence staining were used to determine Cx43/LC3B/OPTN colocalization; 3-MA (autophagy inhibitor) and MG132 (proteasome inhibitor) were used to check the Cx43 degradation pathway in AC-16/H9C2 cells, which underwent programmed electrical stimulation (1 Hz, 10 V, 4 ms, 24 h). Finally, rats with AAV-mediated OPTN overexpression and autophagy regulators were used to detect the effect of OPTN-mediated autophagy on the expression and distribution of Cx43 in AF. Results: OPTN was downregulated in AF (datasets and patient tissues), accompanied by a decrease in LC3B-II/I and an increase in p62. Co-IP confirmed OPTN-Cx43 binding. In OPTN-overexpressing H9C2 cells, MG132 treatment failed to change Cx43 expression level, whereas inhibition of the autophagy-lysosomal pathway by 3-MA led to marked accumulation of Cx43. OPTN overexpression promoted the colocalization of Cx43 with LC3, whereas opposite results were observed in cardiomyocytes transfected with OPTN-specific siRNA. In AF rats, autophagy activation or OPTN overexpression reduced heart weight/body weight ratio, AF duration, left atrial enlargement, structural disorganization, fibrosis, Cx43 lateralization, apoptosis, and oxidative stress. Concurrently, these treatments improved conduction time, conduction velocity, conduction heterogeneity, and AF susceptibility. Conclusions: OPTN-mediated selective autophagy has an important effect on reducing pathological accumulation and abnormal distribution of Cx43 in AF, which provides new mechanistic insights and potential therapeutic targets for AF.
